title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages 782–783). X is a differentiable surface and x a point of X. The notation is read as follows:
- S_x is the circle of tangent half-lines (directions) at x, i.e. (T_xX∖0)/R_{>0}. This is the exceptional circle of the real oriented blow-up at x.
- D_x^* is the germ at x of the punctured neighbourhood X∖{x}.
- T_x ≅ Z is the common fundamental group (Galois group of the universal cover). It is canonically the same for both, since D_x^* retracts onto S_x.
- For an open arc A ∈ 𝒜_x of directions, Ep(A) is the corresponding germ of open sector in D_x^*.

On p.782 a 'corrélation' between a universal cover S_x^~ of S_x and a universal cover D_x^{*~} of D_x^* is defined. It is a compatible family, over the arcs A, of isomorphisms of T_x-torsors S_x^~(A) ≅ D_x^{*~}(Ep(A)). The correlations form a T_x-torsor. The category Corr_x of correlated triples (S^~, D^{*~}, h) maps by the two forgetful functors (117) to Revuniv(S_x) and Revuniv(D_x^*), and both functors are equivalences.

This page proves naturality of the construction under an isomorphism of germs of differentiable surfaces u:(X,x)→(X',x'). Differentiability is used so that u acts on tangent directions.
- (118) u induces three isomorphisms: u_S: S_x ≅ S_{x'} (via the differential), u_{D^*}: D_x^* ≅ D_{x'}^* (a germ of homeomorphism), and u_T: T_x ≅ T_{x'} (free Z-modules of rank 1).
- (119) F(u) is the set of liftings of u_S to the universal covers, and G(u) is the set of liftings of u_{D^*}. Each is a T_x-torsor.
- (120) Claim: there is a canonical isomorphism of T_x-torsors F(u) ≅ G(u). In words: lifting u to the universal cover of the circle of directions is the same as lifting it to the universal cover of the punctured germ.

Proof sketch (completed on p.783). Pull back S_{x'}^~ and D_{x'}^{*~} along u_S and u_{D^*}. By transport of structure the pullbacks carry a correlation h'. Then F(u) = Isom(S_x^~, S_x'^~) and G(u) = Isom(D_x^{*~}, D_x^{*'~}). Both are identified, via the equivalences (117), with the Isom-torsor between the correlated triples (122). The bijection is characterised by compatibility of sections over corresponding sectors (123).

Purpose. This makes 'tangential' data at a puncture intrinsic and functorial. It is a topological/differentiable groundwork for identifying the local fundamental group (inertia) at a point with the π1 of the circle of directions, i.e. for tangential base points, in the 'Longue Marche' setting of surfaces and mapping class groups.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor: F(u) and G(u) are naturally T_{x'}-torsors (or bitorsors). Calling them T_x-torsors implicitly uses u_T, which is harmless.
The differentiability of u is essential for u_S to be defined. A mere homeomorphism of germs does not act on tangent directions. The text uses this correctly but does not comment on it.

ideas.what: Correlation between the universal covers of the circle of directions and of the punctured germ, compatible over sectors; equivalence of the corresponding categories of universal covers
ideas.modern_name: Real oriented blow-up: the boundary circle is homotopy equivalent to the punctured neighbourhood; topological tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (A'Campo / real oriented blow-up); tangential base points: Deligne 1989
ideas.where_published: Tangential base points are mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific formalism is not known in print

ideas.what: Canonical bijection between liftings of a germ-isomorphism to the two universal covers (naturality of the correlation under diffeomorphisms of germs)
ideas.modern_name: Naturality / transport of structure for tangential base points

missed.claim: A careful, torsor-theoretic, functorial treatment of the identification between universal covers of the punctured germ and of the circle of tangent directions. This is a topological prototype of tangential base points, developed within the Longue Marche material on surfaces and the Teichmüller tower.
missed.quote: il revient au même de relever u_S en un iso. u_{S~} : S_x~ → S_x'~, ou de relever u_{D*} en u_{D*~} : D_x*~ → D_x'*~
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's own handling of tangential base points before Deligne's 1989 formalism. The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine naturality argument. Historically it illustrates Grothendieck's topological groundwork for tangential base points, but nothing here is mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'sans [?] soigneusement [?] pour pour' is uncertain. The sense is that the constructions are intrinsic and hence functorial (transportable) for an isomorphism of germs; 'pour pour' is a duplicated word in the manuscript.
The third element of the triples is likely 'h_x' (the correlation), not 'i_x', consistent with pages 782–783.
The arrow in (X,x) → (X',x') carries 'u' above and '~' below.
